title: QOR host protocol, version 1
description: What a product the launcher started (QQ Studio, first) and the launcher say to each other (ADR-046, ADR-088). Each frame is a 4-byte big-endian length and then one UTF-8 JSON object of at most 1 MiB. The product opens with hello and the launcher answers welcome, or an error and closes the channel; then the product sends requests, one at a time, each answered by a result or an error with its id. Unknown fields are ignored. The golden/ folder holds frames the launcher's tests read (src-tauri/src/host/tests.rs).

hello.description: Product to launcher, first frame and only once. token is the 64 hex characters the product read from its stdin; it is good once, for 30 seconds from the spawn.

product.description: The product's id, which must be the one the launcher started (qq-studio).

request.description: Product to launcher: a typed intent. method is one of the capabilities the welcome announced.

params.description: Commit everything changed in the project. Answered {commit: <hex id>} or {commit: null} when nothing changed; refused (code qontrol) when Qontrol's guard warns about a file.

Publish the commit HEAD points at as the project's Cartridge (ADR-088): answered {action: minted|revised, receipt} after the launcher's dialog, or {action: unchanged, collection, item, name, commit} with no dialog when the Cartridge is already at HEAD.

welcome.description: Launcher to product, after a good hello. session is never logged.

result.description: Launcher to product: the request with this id, done.

error.description: Launcher to product: the request with this id refused, or, with id null, the handshake refused and the channel closed. code is stable (unsupported_method, bad_request, protocol_mismatch, not_authorised, or one of the launcher's own: declined, vault_locked, qontrol, rpc, …); message is a sentence for the person.
